summary.headline: The Southborough School Committee reviewed town budget guidelines requiring two FY28 budget models and drafted annual budget priorities.
summary.summary: The Southborough School Committee convened to review directives and timelines for the FY28 budget cycle. The town instructed the district to prepare both a level-service budget with identified efficiencies and a level-funded budget. The committee also refined its FY28 budget priorities, focusing on maintaining educational programs, managing special education and healthcare costs, and expanding the district capital plan to an 8-to-10-year outlook.

topics.title: FY28 budget process and guidelines
topics.summary: District administrators outlined town instructions requiring departments to build two budget proposals for FY28: a level-service budget that incorporates identified efficiencies, and a level-funded budget that caps non-salary expenses at FY27 levels. The presentation highlighted budget variables including inflation, special education tuitions, rising utility supplier rates, and potential operational transition costs tied to the Neary School building project. Committee members discussed the budget calendar, which targets a preliminary presentation on November 9, 2026, a recommended budget on January 13, 2027, and a committee vote on February 10, 2027.
key_details: The 10-year average budget increase for Southborough Public Schools is 3.02 percent.
The town directive instructs departments not to consider new positions or programs.
Budget A requires non-salary lines to be benchmarked to FY26 actual spending, while Budget B caps non-salary lines at FY27 levels.
Special education transportation costs have stabilized due to a new in-house contract model.
The recommended FY28 budget is scheduled to be voted on by the committee on February 10, 2027, ahead of March Town Meeting.
topics.outcome: Administrators will proceed with preparing both level-service and level-funded budget proposals for committee review in November.
topics.why_it_matters: The town's dual-budget mandate requires school officials to evaluate service reductions and cost efficiencies that could directly affect school staffing and operations.

topics.title: Draft FY28 budget priorities
topics.summary: The committee reviewed and edited draft budget priorities that will guide the superintendent and administration in developing the FY28 operating budget. Priorities include maintaining high-quality education, preserving student-facing programs, monitoring student-to-teacher ratios under district class size guidelines, and collaborating with town officials to manage healthcare costs. Members agreed to extend the district capital planning goal from a five-year window to an 8-to-10-year horizon to better forecast large facility needs such as roofs and HVAC systems.
key_details: Language was refined to call for developing a budget that is both fiscally and educationally responsible.
Priorities emphasize protecting elementary world language, health and science, and multilingual learner supports.
The capital plan goal was modified to cover an 8-to-10-year outlook rather than five years.
The committee discussed ensuring capacity built through grant funding, such as the PRISM grant, remains sustainable after grant expiration.
topics.outcome: Administrators will update the draft budget priorities document for a second read and potential approval at the October 14, 2026 meeting.
topics.why_it_matters: These goals establish the formal criteria the school administration must use to balance academic standards with municipal tax constraints.

topics.title: Town government structure survey inquiry
topics.summary: A committee member raised a procedural question regarding an email survey distributed in September by the Town Government Study Committee. The member expressed concern that the School Committee as an elected town body was not directly included in the recipient list, although several members received it individually or through other town roles.
key_details: The survey was issued on September 11, 2026, regarding town government structure.
The chair agreed to verify whether the School Committee received formal outreach.
